svg.title: Source–readout formulation. Equation (RUN5) recovers the first quantitative clause of the supplied public conclusion (Section 4) as a property of the calibrated realized history: the readout Readslope(N, p) = βN,p/ log(h−1 N ) converges to s uniformly in p, with witnesses the calendar c and the trajectories of Theorems 14.24 and 14.29. It is stronger than writing down the reference line bβm, since it controls the actual finite-cutoffcoupling. The regulator coupling gi of (RUN6) is defined from the inverse action coefficient. Its leading logarithm does not by itself identify it with a coupling defined by a physical position-space observable; that identification and its normalization are a separate result of the trace and Ward calculation (Section 23.1). The lift keeps the two notions as two different readers of the same realized history, and no physical significance is attached to (RUN6) beyond the stated limit.
